newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end lower, seen range-bound.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end lower, seen range-bound.

text.p: Chilean stocks ended sharply lower in moderate trade on profit-taking with the market seen rangebound in coming sessions, said traders.
"Momentum has died down in the Chilean market. Stocks will continue trading in a tight band between 108 and 110 points," said Nicolas Allende, a trader at ING Barings.
The 40-share index ended down 2.25 percent at 108.38 points. The general shed 1.04 percent at 5,185.85 points amid volume of 12.4 billion pesos.
Brokers reported turnover dominated profit-taking by foreign investors and book trading by local players.
Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts were also hurt by Wall Street's slide, dragging local stock prices down in their wake, said dealers.
Traders said 1996 profit figures from telecom CTC, the first large company to issue its earnings, were at the lower end of market expectations.
CTC, which reported a 30 percent jump in earnings to 150.5 billion pesos, lost 1.74 percent to 2,545 pesos.
Other losers included electricity stocks, with Enersis tumbling 3.56 percent to 244 pesos, and Endesa off 2.03 percent at 241 pesos.
Winners included fishing company Coloso, up 1.66 percent at 275 pesos and power utility Chilquinta, up 1.52 percent at 2,010 pesos.
